prompt:
Implement this service.

<spec>
name: ttl-cache-service
description: An in-memory key-value cache where entries expire after a TTL.
endpoints:
- method: GET
  path: /health
- method: GET
  path: /metrics
- method: PUT
  path: /cache/{key}
  description: 'body {value: string, ttl_seconds: int > 0}; 200 or 201 on success;
    400 if value missing or ttl_seconds <= 0 or malformed JSON'
- method: GET
  path: /cache/{key}
  description: 200 {key, value}; 404 if absent or expired
- method: DELETE
  path: /cache/{key}
  description: 200 or 204 if deleted; 404 if absent
metrics:
- name: cache_entries
  type: gauge
  help: Live (unexpired) entries
- name: cache_hits_total
  type: counter
  help: Successful reads
- name: cache_misses_total
  type: counter
  help: Reads of absent or expired keys
behaviors:
- Expiry is evaluated lazily on read AND by a background sweeper so cache_entries
  stays accurate
probes:
- method: PUT
  path: /cache/k1
  expect_status:
  - 200
  - 201
  body: '{"value": "v", "ttl_seconds": 60}'
- method: GET
  path: /cache/k1
  expect_status:
  - 200
- method: GET
  path: /cache/nope
  expect_status:
  - 404
- method: PUT
  path: /cache/k2
  expect_status:
  - 400
  body: '{"ttl_seconds": 5}'
- method: PUT
  path: /cache/k3
  expect_status:
  - 400
  body: '{"value": "v", "ttl_seconds": 0}'
- method: DELETE
  path: /cache/k1
  expect_status:
  - 200
  - 204
- method: GET
  path: /cache/k1
  expect_status:
  - 404
</spec>

Already provided by templates (do NOT write or register these):
- main.go: `func newServer() http.Handler` serves GET /health and GET /metrics, then calls
  `registerRoutes(mux)`. Do not register /health or /metrics yourself.
- metrics.go: Prometheus variables you must keep up to date from your handlers:
- cacheEntries  (gauge) -> exposed as `cache_entries`; use Set/Inc/Dec/Add
- cacheHitsTotal  (counter) -> exposed as `cache_hits_total`; use Inc/Add
- cacheMissesTotal  (counter) -> exposed as `cache_misses_total`; use Inc/Add

You must write these files:
1. handlers.go - defines `func registerRoutes(mux *http.ServeMux)` that registers ONLY these routes:
   - PUT /cache/{key}  body {value: string, ttl_seconds: int > 0}; 200 or 201 on success; 400 if value missing or ttl_seconds <= 0 or malformed JSON
   - GET /cache/{key}  200 {key, value}; 404 if absent or expired
   - DELETE /cache/{key}  200 or 204 if deleted; 404 if absent
   Keep state in memory (you may add store.go). Return JSON with proper status codes; reject
   malformed input with 400. The behaviors in the spec are verified at runtime.
2. handlers_test.go - at least 3 `func TestXxx(t *testing.T)` functions using
   net/http/httptest against `newServer()`. Never bind real ports; tests must finish in seconds.
3. README.md - must contain: an "## Endpoints" section listing EVERY spec endpoint (including
   /health and /metrics) as `METHOD /path` in backticks, and a "## Metrics" section listing EVERY
   metric name in backticks. Only document things that actually exist.
